interpretation: Each creation path is converted only when its actual constructor and real journey prove a chain or the required refusal. Legacy paths retain their existing behavior for now; reasons are explicit.
Key rotation, team/session/encryption keys and reused projections are not new identity ancestry.
Cloud coverage belongs to the application repository. Public external runtime paths remain listed with their repository owner.
The one primitive-use check permits shared verifiers and explicitly named released legacy files. It does not pin call counts or claim complete release qualification.

creation_paths.reason: Bare DID genesis validates the new key proof (awid/src/awid_service/routes/did.py:302), independently of ID-certificate enrollment. The real constructor journey proves a registered, unenrolled did:aw remains unknown/unregistered_identity (scripts/cross-registry-human-journey.py:269,283). This is an intentional bare-ID path, not chain issuance or a required ancestry refusal; enrollment must occur through a separate parent constructor.

GenerateKeypair and SaveSigningKey only generate/store agent key material (cli/go/awid/keys.go:20,52); they cannot establish parent authority. Real parent constructors using those keys are covered by CLI.CREATE.PARENT and CLI.INVITE.LOCAL. The helper itself has no ancestry constructor or chain-or-refusal journey; human keychain custody remains separate.

aw id human init --domain D --as-root creates the human key in the OS keychain, registers its did:aw with the human's own proof and has the local namespace controller issue its certificate, recorded before release. The cross-registry real-DNS journey (scripts/cross-registry-human-journey.py) proves it through a real Secret Service and a PTY, after its wrong-controller refusals, with outsiders verifying the human as nearest_human.

The first local-team bootstrap creates a local member with the team controller and persists its signing key/team certificate, without an ID-parent issuance step (cli/go/cmd/aw/init_local.go:164,193,211). Its real quickstart retry journey tests connection recovery (scripts/e2e-oss-user-journey.sh:2927), not a parent chain. Missing: an attributed local-init constructor and real chain-or-required-refusal journey; a human-less local team may still coordinate as unknown.

The BYOD wizard prepares a bare identity, optionally registers its global DID/address, then bootstraps membership (cli/go/cmd/aw/onboarding_wizard.go:422,457,479). It does not select an ID parent or install a chain. CLI.CREATE.PARENT proves the explicit id-create flags, not this wizard entry point. Missing: wizard parent issuance/installation and its own real chain-or-required-refusal journey.

The signup wizard generates a key, optionally registers its DID, calls cli-signup and persists a team certificate (cli/go/cmd/aw/onboarding_wizard.go:137,671,705). This separate signup path does not consume the hosted ID-tree creation response used by id create --org/API-key init. Missing: signup-chain consumption and a real wizard journey proving the selected parent or required refusal; account labels cannot supply it.

Bootstrap redemption generates a key, optionally registers its DID, validates the returned member certificate and connects (cli/go/cmd/aw/connect.go:77,111,122,132). It does not install an ID-parent chain. Missing: a redemption response/consumer binding ancestry to that exact child and a real token-redemption chain-or-required-refusal journey. The token itself is not ancestry evidence.

The landed consumer independently reads the selected team, retains the creation response and verifies/registers/installs the returned chain (cli/go/cmd/aw/init_apikey.go:169,276,289). Shared recovery tests use fixture status/registration HTTP handlers and a static TXT resolver (cli/go/cmd/aw/hosted_creation_install_test.go:151,185,219). Missing on OSS main: a coherent published CLI/Cloud/AWID journey of API-key local/global creation under the hosted root, no_human verification, and unchanged registry-failure resume. API-key identity must never imply a human parent.

Without parent flags, id create registers the bare DID/address and writes the key; ID-chain installation runs only when a parent was explicitly selected (cli/go/cmd/aw/id_create.go:177,238,303). The real-DNS journey now asserts this path has no chain and reports unknown/unregistered_identity (scripts/cross-registry-human-journey.py:269,279). Unenrolled creation is covered; it is not an ancestry conversion. Explicit enrolled creation is CLI.CREATE.PARENT.

aw id create --human-parent <did:aw> or --root-parent installs the agent's chain at creation: the named human or the namespace root issues it after verifying current status, records it before release, and the agent registers it with its own key; a parent that cannot issue leaves no agent. The cross-registry real-DNS journey proves both parents and a failed registration resuming with the same ID, key and certificate and one issuance entry; outsiders verify the human-parented agents as nearest_human and the root agent as no_human.

The request exchange: aw id child invite/receive/pending/show/approve/refuse under an explicitly selected issuer, and aw id parent request/import for a prepared human or the current agent, including the root-issued first human; a human child is approved only by a confirmed terminal answer. The cross-registry real-DNS journey (scripts/cross-registry-human-journey.py, AWEB_CROSS_REGISTRY_CSR=1) proves it across separate requester and root machines: a declined fingerprint signs nothing and leaves the request pending, the matching fingerprint is approved with y over a PTY, and the default import registers the human with the same invitation, with outsiders verifying it as nearest_human.

The person-authorized --org consumer selects the account human independently, retains the full creation response, and fresh-verifies/installs its chain (cli/go/cmd/aw/id_create_hosted.go:168,266,282,300). Missing on OSS main: a coherent published-cohort real human-session Cloud creation journey proving the selected human, required refusal without fallback, original-key/certificate registry resume and outsider verification. The shared fixture recovery test at cli/go/cmd/aw/hosted_creation_install_test.go:151 is not that journey.

The native owner consumer selects its actual issuer, issues/registers the child before Cloud admission, and requires the response to accept that same chain (cli/go/cmd/aw/id_create_hosted.go:163,210,227,294; cli/go/cmd/aw/id_create_owner.go:32). Missing on OSS main: a coherent published-cohort real owner-authorized --org journey proving nearest_human/no_human as appropriate, unchanged recovery, and independent identity versus refused membership. Fixture owner checks (cli/go/cmd/aw/hosted_creation_install_test.go:254) do not qualify the Cloud constructor.

Local identity creation composes the real inviter child exchange; CoreDNS verifies immediate human attribution, purpose and outsider Go/Python verification. Chainless inviters remain unknown; existing global acceptance preserves enrollment and chain. CoreDNS also verifies that an outstanding invite from a revoked inviter cannot be accepted and the inviter cannot create a new local invite, with no child identity or issuer-record changes.

The landed consumer requires an issue-time preview and pins issuer/domain/kind/mode before accept, retains the response and installs only its verified chain (cli/go/cmd/aw/hosted_invite_creation.go:70; cli/go/cmd/aw/id_team.go:2198,2303,2328). Its recovery tests use vector-backed status/accept servers and static TXT (cli/go/cmd/aw/hosted_invite_creation_test.go:115,126,145). Missing on OSS main: the published-cohort real Cloud issue/preview/accept journey for native and host-managed agents, local/global children, per-child registration UUID and unchanged no-second-accept resume; unavailable preview must refuse.

This team-controller operation generates a replacement local did:key, not an ID-parent certificate (cli/go/cmd/aw/team_replace_key.go:329). The real stack explicitly checks the replacement remains unknown/legacy_no_chain (cli/go/e2e/team_create_flow_e2e_test.go:232,292). The root-admits-replacement-human J10 case (scripts/cross-registry-human-journey.py:453) is a different constructor. Missing here: explicit new-parent issuance and a real chain-or-required-refusal replacement journey; never inherit the old key ancestry.

Connect now independently verifies the member binding and ID chain before projecting team/agent/workspace state (server/src/aweb/team_auth_deps.py:285; server/src/aweb/routes/connect.py:483,491). The real-DNS journey proves human/root chains survive a successful connection (scripts/e2e-cross-registry-messaging.sh:480,488,495), but those aw who assertions read the client chain; they do not distinguish a connect endpoint that skips its ancestry gate. Missing: a real connect-specific journey proving invalid/revoked enrolled ancestry refuses before projection effects, alongside the valid neighbor. This is a proof gap, not an absent shared verifier or permission to mint/re-parent on reconnect.
Actual parent signs coordinator/seat/sub-seat; deployment team root is not automatically the identity parent. This creation path has no landed per-path chain-or-refusal journey proof yet.
Unattended owner-ID to resident link; no human gesture per owned spawn. This creation path has no landed per-path chain-or-refusal journey proof yet.
Unsigned runtime parent metadata does not establish ancestry. The external runtime provider has not supplied a landed chain-or-refusal creation journey.
